soil-env-216.q: Why does a septic tank need pumping out from time to time?
soil-env-216.a: Sludge builds up faster than it decomposes, so it is pumped out by vacuum truck.

soil-env-190.q: What body did the partnership's First Plenary Assembly establish?
soil-env-190.a: The Intergovernmental Technical Panel on Soils, whose experts advise the partnership on science.

soil-env-019.q: Why does phosphorus reach water mostly through erosion, while nitrate travels in water?
soil-env-019.a: Many forms of phosphorus adsorb onto soil particles, whereas nitrate moves in water flowing through the soil, such as tile drainage.

soil-env-033.q: Why can fungi break down pollutants that bacteria degrade poorly?
soil-env-033.a: Their non-specific enzymes attack substances such as pharmaceuticals and fragrances.

soil-env-020.q: Why does excess phosphorus drive eutrophication in lakes but nitrogen in the sea?
soil-env-020.a: Phosphorus usually limits plant growth in fresh water and nitrogen in the sea.

soil-env-026.q: Why can the same amount of a contaminant be toxic in one soil and harmless in another?
soil-env-026.a: Soil pH, organic matter and texture change how mobile, bioavailable and toxic a pollutant is, so risk assessment must be soil-specific.

soil-env-010.q: How does biomagnification differ from bioaccumulation?
soil-env-010.a: Bioaccumulation is build-up within one organism from its food and surroundings; biomagnification is the increase across food-chain levels.

soil-env-055.q: What is the main advantage of biostimulation?
soil-env-055.a: Native microbes, already suited to the subsurface and spread through it, do the work.

soil-env-025.q: How does biosparging differ from bioventing?
soil-env-025.a: Bioventing aerates the unsaturated zone, while biosparging targets the saturated zone below the water table.

soil-env-053.q: Why is landfarming unsuitable for metal-polluted soil?
soil-env-053.a: Inorganic contaminants are not degraded by it.

soil-env-041.q: How do plant roots help microbes clean contaminated soil?
soil-env-041.a: Roots release carbohydrates and acids that stimulate microbes, which then biodegrade the contaminants.

soil-env-204.q: Why can a factory outfall be modelled as a mathematical point?
soil-env-204.a: A point source has negligible extent, unlike nonpoint and area sources.

soil-env-036.q: How do mycorrhizal fungi lower the bioavailability of heavy metals?
soil-env-036.a: They produce proteins that bind the metals.

soil-env-051.q: Why has phytomining had limited commercial success?
soil-env-051.a: A review judged it slow and inefficient; by mid-2024 one nickel project had extracted less than a kilo of usable nickel.

soil-hist-040.q: Which classification system has had its editions launched at World Congresses of Soil Science?
soil-hist-040.a: The World Reference Base, first at Montpellier in 1998 and in its fourth edition at Glasgow in 2022.

soil-hist-043.q: What accreditation can members of the Australian Society of Soil Science gain?
soil-hist-043.a: They can become Certified Professional Soil Scientists.

soil-hist-029.q: Why did Marbut base classification on morphology rather than genesis?
soil-hist-029.a: He saw theories of soil genesis as ephemeral and dynamic.

soil-hist-046.q: What did the Park Grass Experiment reveal about ordinary field trials?
soil-hist-046.a: They probably underestimate long-term threats such as soil acidification.

soil-hist-030.q: Which soil-forming factor gained much more weight after 1940?
soil-hist-030.a: Time, with geomorphology used to find how long material has undergone soil formation.

soil-hist-004.q: Why is Liebig called the father of the fertilizer industry?
soil-hist-004.a: He stressed nitrogen and minerals as essential plant nutrients and popularized the law of the minimum.

soil-hist-008.q: What did Glinka's 1908 soil science textbook contain for the first time?
soil-hist-008.a: The first schematic soil map of the world.

soil-hist-024.q: When did Guy Smith's soil classification become official?
soil-hist-024.a: In 1965, after more than 15 years of work; it was published in 1975 as Soil Taxonomy.

soil-hist-073.q: What did Boussingault show about legumes in a crop rotation?
soil-hist-073.a: Soil nitrogen rises after legume crops.

soil-hist-014.q: What did chemoautotrophy overturn about how autotrophs get energy?
soil-hist-014.a: Autotrophs were thought to get energy only from light; some instead oxidize hydrogen sulfide or ammonium.

soil-hist-075.q: What did Hiltner mean by the rhizosphere?
soil-hist-075.a: The soil directly affected by root secretions and their microorganisms.

soil-hist-048.q: Which two bodies merged to form the Soil Science Society of America?
soil-hist-048.a: The Soils Section of the American Society of Agronomy and the American Soil Survey Association.

soil-hist-049.a: The World Soil Information Service (WoSIS) and SoilGrids.

soil-hist-055.q: Why does the society keep standard samples of humic and fulvic acids?
soil-hist-055.a: So scientists in many countries can work from the same reference materials, drawn from leonardite, river water, a mineral soil and peat.

soil-hist-059.q: How does lunar soil form differently from Earth's soil?
soil-hist-059.a: Mainly by mechanical weathering, as impacts and charged particles grind rock finer, not by oxygen, water and life.

soil-hist-079.q: Why do young crater rays on the Moon fade over time?
soil-hist-079.a: Space weathering makes lunar soil darker and redder as it matures.

soil-hist-083.q: How can oxygen be extracted from lunar regolith?
soil-hist-083.a: By heating its iron oxide above 900 °C in hydrogen gas.

soil-hist-080.q: Why does impact debris build up as regolith on airless bodies?
soil-hist-080.a: Lacking an atmosphere, they have almost no erosion to remove it.
